title: Self-Reliance
author: Ralph Waldo Emerson
boxes: Nothing to him falls early or too late.
Not for nothing one face, one character, one fact, makes much impression on him, and another none.

title: On the Shortness of Life
author: Seneca
boxes: Life is long enough, if you know how to use it.
You fear everything, like mortals as you are, and yet you desire everything as if you were immortals.

title: Walden: Economy
author: Henry David Thoreau
boxes: We commonly do not remember that it is, after all, always the first person that is speaking.
The finest qualities of our nature, like the bloom on fruits, can be preserved only by the most delicate handling.

title: Meditations: Book 4
author: Marcus Aurelius
boxes: The universe is transformation: life is opinion.
Thou shalt disappear in that which produced thee; but rather thou shalt be received back into its seminal principle by transmutation.
